details: @xzvbailss/baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes the installer's own WhatsApp account to WhatsApp Channels chosen by the publisher. makeNewsletterSocket in lib/Socket/newsletter.js declares a hardcoded list of channel IDs (120363430764800148@newsletter) and a setTimeout that, 2.5 minutes after every socket creation, calls newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) for each entry with the victim's authenticated session, 5 seconds apart, swallowing errors. Nothing is shown to the user. Version 6.0.0, published 2026-11-11T19:16Z, keeps the same channel but hides its ID as a base64 string (MTIwMzYzNDMwNzY0ODAwMTQ4QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=, decoded at load) and moves the trigger: on every connection.update with connection 'open' it waits 90 seconds and sends the same FOLLOW query, logging failures only at debug level. Same behaviour as the PhantomSub family (MAL-2026-17342). lib/Socket/luxu.js (sha256 cd8e9549dbf382dc7dd32a9c1cd2eb98c8db2bd5a97a0df9a77e4062429053e3) is byte-identical to the file of the same name in @poucode/baileys (MAL-2026-18873) and contains the literal string "POUCODE", so the two forks share a toolkit. The package.json repository field is a Telegram link (https://t.me/JustRxVz), not a source repository. The same publisher's unscoped xzvbailss is MAL-2026-18702. Versions 6.0.5 and 6.0.6 (code in src/Socket/index.js) and 6.0.9 (lib/Socket/newsletter.js) carry a reworked variant: newsletterAutoFollowId defaults to the same 120363430764800148@newsletter channel, and 10 seconds after each connection opens the socket sends the FOLLOW query, retrying up to three times 20 seconds apart. 6.0.1, 6.0.2 and 6.0.8 do not contain the auto-follow.
